definitions.explanation: The quality of being young or childlike, whether an endearing innocence or an immaturity in attitude. The noun form of {幼|おさな}い.

examples.japanese: {顔|かお}に{幼|おさな}さが{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: A youthful look still remains on her face.

examples.japanese: {考|かんが}え{方|かた}に{幼|おさな}さを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I sensed a certain immaturity in his way of thinking.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{言葉|ことば}には{幼|おさな}さと{素直|すなお}さが{同時|どうじ}に{表|あらわ}れていた。
examples.english: His words showed both immaturity and honesty at the same time.

notes:
The noun form of the i-adjective {幼|おさな}い (young, childish), made with the {〜さ} suffix. It can be positive (endearing innocence, a youthful appearance) or negative (immaturity of thought), depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幼|おさな}さが{残|のこ}る: retain a childlike quality
- {幼|おさな}さを{感|かん}じる: sense immaturity / youthfulness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {若|わか}さ: youth — about being young in years; {幼|おさな}さ suggests something more childlike or unfinished
